Definition: middle voice from G4253 and G2564; to call forth to oneself (challenge), i.e. (by implication) to irritate:--provoke.
BiblicalUsage: Prokaleomai means to call forth, to challenge, to provoke. Paul uses it once, in the warning against vainglory: let us not be desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe provoking is vainglory's child, and the church that stops provoking starts loving.
